title: Halves and Quarters
seo_title: Halves and Quarters – Primary 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify halves and quarters of shapes and objects; share objects into two and four equal groups. (summary of the NERDC Primary 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 maths worksheets on halves and quarters: equal parts, half of a shape, quarter of a shape, half and quarter of a group, and stories. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A half is one of 2 equal parts.
  • A quarter is one of 4 equal parts.
  • To find half of 8 sweets, share them into 2 equal groups: 4 each.

Examples

Example

Half of 10

Share into 2 groups

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Parts that are not equalHalves must be the same size.
Thinking a quarter is bigger than a halfA quarter is smaller.
Counting all the partsA half is just one part.

sets.title: Half and quarter of a group

items.q: Find half of 4 counters.
items.e: Share the 4 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 2. 2 + 2 = 4. So half of 4 is 2.

items.q: Find half of 6 sweets.
items.e: Share the 6 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 3. 3 + 3 = 6. So half of 6 is 3.

items.q: Find half of 8 counters.
items.e: Share the 8 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 4. 4 + 4 = 8. So half of 8 is 4.

items.q: Find half of 10 sweets.
items.e: Share the 10 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 5. 5 + 5 = 10. So half of 10 is 5.

items.q: Find half of 12 counters.
items.e: Share the 12 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 6. 6 + 6 = 12. So half of 12 is 6.

items.q: Find half of 14 sweets.
items.e: Share the 14 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 7. 7 + 7 = 14. So half of 14 is 7.

items.q: Find half of 16 counters.
items.e: Share the 16 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 8. 8 + 8 = 16. So half of 16 is 8.

items.q: Find half of 20 sweets.
items.e: Share the 20 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 10. 10 + 10 = 20. So half of 20 is 10.

items.q: Find a quarter of 4 sweets.
items.e: Share the 4 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 1. 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. So a quarter of 4 is 1.

items.q: Find a quarter of 8 counters.
items.e: Share the 8 counters into 4 equal groups. Each group has 2. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. So a quarter of 8 is 2.

items.q: Find a quarter of 12 sweets.
items.e: Share the 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 3. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. So a quarter of 12 is 3.

items.q: Find a quarter of 16 sweets.
items.e: Share the 16 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 4. 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16. So a quarter of 16 is 4.

items.q: Find a quarter of 20 counters.
items.e: Share the 20 counters into 4 equal groups. Each group has 5. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20. So a quarter of 20 is 5.

items.q: What part of the counters is in the green box?
items.e: There are 6 counters in 2 equal groups of 3. 1 group is green. So the green group is half of the counters.

items.q: What part of the sweets is in the green box?
items.e: There are 16 sweets in 2 equal groups of 8. 1 group is green. So the green group is half of the sweets.

items.q: What part of the sweets is in the green box?
items.e: There are 12 sweets in 4 equal groups of 3. 1 group is green. So the green group is a quarter of the sweets.

items.q: What part of the counters is in the green box?
items.e: There are 8 counters in 4 equal groups of 2. 1 group is green. So the green group is a quarter of the counters.

items.q: What part of the counters is in the green box?
items.e: There are 2 groups, but one has 5 and one has 3. They are not equal, so the green group is not a half.

items.q: 12 counters are in 3 equal groups. Is the green box a quarter?
items.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 equal groups. Here there are only 3 groups. There are 4 counters in the box, but that does not make it a quarter.

items.q: Uju and Dayo share 10 sweets. Uju gets 6. Dayo gets 4. Do they each get half?
items.e: Half of 10 is 5. Halves are equal: 5 and 5. 6 and 4 are not equal.

items.q: Joy eats the green slice of pizza. How much of the pizza does she eat?
items.e: The pizza has 4 equal slices. Joy eats 1 of them. That is a quarter.

items.q: Ikenna has the green part of the cake. How much does he have?
items.e: The cake has 2 equal parts. Ikenna has 1 of them. That is a half.

items.q: Femi breaks this chocolate bar in half. How many squares are in each half?
items.e: The bar has 8 squares. Half of 8 is 4, because 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Yusuf has these sweets. He gives half to Ngozi. How many sweets does Ngozi get?
items.e: There are 18 sweets. Share them into 2 equal groups. 9 + 9 = 18. Ngozi gets 9.

items.q: Uju has half of a cake. Yusuf has a quarter of the same cake. Who has more?
items.e: A half is 1 of 2 equal parts. A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts. 4 parts are smaller. So Uju has more.

items.q: Which is bigger: half of an orange or a quarter of the same orange?
items.e: 4 is more than 2, but more parts means smaller parts. So a half is bigger.

items.q: Temi shares a pizza equally with 1 friend. How much does each one get?
items.e: Temi and 1 friend are 2 people. 2 equal parts are halves. Each one gets a half.

items.q: Kelechi shares a cake equally with 3 friends. How much does each one get?
items.e: Kelechi and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal parts are quarters. Do not forget to count Kelechi.

items.q: Amaka and Victor share 10 grapes equally. How many grapes does each one get?
items.e: Share 10 into 2 equal groups. 5 + 5 = 10. Each one gets 5.

items.q: 4 friends share 8 strawberries equally. How many does each friend get?
items.e: Share 8 into 4 equal groups. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. A quarter of 8 is 2.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into halves. B is cut into fourths. A half is bigger than a fourth, so A is bigger. (4 is more than 2, but more shares means smaller shares.)

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into fourths. B is cut into halves. A half is bigger than a fourth, so B is bigger.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: Both squares are cut into fourths. Each shaded share is a fourth of the same square. A triangle and a small square can be the same size.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: Both squares are cut into halves. Half of a square is the same size, whether the cut goes down the middle or corner to corner.

items.q: The circles are the same size. Which circle has the smallest shares?
items.e: Circle D is cut into fourths. That is the most shares. More shares means smaller shares.

items.q: The rectangles are the same size. Which rectangle has the biggest shares?
items.e: Rectangle C is cut into halves. The others are cut into fourths. Fewer shares means bigger shares.

items.q: Which is bigger: half of a pizza or a fourth of the same pizza?
items.e: A half is 1 of 2 equal shares. A fourth is 1 of 4 equal shares. More shares means smaller shares. So half is bigger.

items.q: Which is smaller: a quarter of a cake or half of the same cake?
items.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 shares. Half is 1 of 2 shares. 4 shares are smaller, so a quarter is smaller.

items.q: You cut the same pie into more equal shares. What happens to each share?
items.e: The pie stays the same. More shares means each share is smaller.

items.q: Uju cuts her pancake into halves. Kayode cuts the same size pancake into fourths. Whose pieces are bigger?
items.e: Kayode has more pieces, so his pieces are smaller. Halves are bigger than fourths, so Uju’s pieces are bigger.
